summary: Client/server one-frame-like request to create (register) an entity's physics from an already built physics object; handled by ls::PhysicsLoaderSystem::ProcessCreateRequests / FlushCreateQueue (Toolkit GameEngine.dll+0x789E00 / +0x788F00) and read by phx::PhysXDisableSimulationSystem::ProcessChangedClusters. Not a one-frame type by registry (removed by the loader). Seen alive after level changes and in new areas (dialog trees).

fields.name: PhysicsObject
fields.evidence: Windows bg3.exe+0x3B0E120 (= Toolkit ls::PhysicsLoaderSystem::FlushCreateQueue, GameEngine.dll+0x788F00) adds the component with its creator bg3.exe+0x3B12080 (0x10 bytes, zeroed) and writes the queued request's 8-byte object here ('*puVar14 = *puVar25'); when an entity's request is replaced or the entity is dead the old object is handed to a manager's virtual slot +0x18 (Toolkit: SavegameObjectFactory::IsReserved on the ObjectHandle), and in the drain loop the 0x10-stride column of this component (the type that is removed right after with FUN_1440103b0) is released the same way and cleared. Live: heap pointers (an ls::PhysicsObject, cf. macOS ProcessUnloadRequests' Span<ls::PhysicsObject*>).

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x3B0E120 copies the request's 4-byte value (request +0x10 in the Toolkit queue element) here ('*(uint *)(puVar14 + 1) = ...'); meaning not established. Live: always 1.

fields.name: _PadC
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the creator, never written by the filler; padding to 16.

open_questions: Meaning of the 4-byte value at +8 (always 1 live).
The +0 pointer's class is named only through macOS (ls::PhysicsObject*) and the Toolkit's ObjectHandle parameter.
second_pass: Settled from the Windows FlushCreateQueue bg3.exe+0x3B0E120: it creates the component (bg3.exe+0x3B12080), stores an 8-byte object at +0 and a 4-byte value at +8, and its drain loop releases +0 of the 0x10-stride column before removing the component - which also proves the column is this component.
